hints.content:
The function $h$ is negative $($i.e. $h(x)<0)$ whenever its graph is below the $x$-axis.

This is because the negative $y$-values are below the $x$-axis, and $y=h(x)$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by one. The graph of the function y equals h of x is below the x-axis from x equals negative five to x equals negative four. It is above the x-axis from x equals negative four to x equals negative two and one-half. It is below the x-axis from x equals negative two and one-half to x equals negative one. It is above the x-axis from x equals negative one to x equals one. It is below the x-axis from x equals one to x equals two and one-half. It is above the x-axis from x equals two and one-half to x equals four. It is below the x-axis after x equals four. The function increases from x equals negative five to x equals negative three and one-quarter. The function decreases from x equals negative three and one-quarter to x equals negative one and one-half. The function increases from x equals negative one and one-half to x equals zero. It is decreasing from x equals zero to x equals one and one-half. It is increasing from x equals one and one-half to x equals three and one-quarter. It is decreasing from x equals three and one-quarter to x equals five. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative five to x equals negative four, from x equals negative two and one-quarter to x equals negative one, from x equals one to x equals two and one-quarter, and from x equals four to x equals five.

hints.content: Out of our options, the only correct interval is $-2<x<-1$.
